cand.title: OENOVITI International Symposium and General Assembly 2027

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Pierre-Louis Teissedre is verified as Head of OENOVITI International / coordinator; the Bordeaux Coordination Office explicitly handles event organization. Isabel Baehler, head of Changins general secretariat, is a verified local institutional routing contact. Eric Pasche, Changins intendant, is a local facilities/logistics routing contact. None is publicly verified as the 2027 accommodation contracting buyer; participants book their own lodging.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced for 19–21 May 2027 in Nyon, Switzerland, within the requested horizon. Theme: Viticulture 2030: Addressing Environmental, Social and Human Challenges. Agroscope lists 08:30–18:00 and registration opening 1 December 2026 at 00:01; these are distinct from the activity dates. No 2028 edition announcement was found in the official event listing reviewed.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: Nyon / La Côte demand is territorially appropriate for YOTEL Geneva Lake in Founex. The realistic offer is optional participant accommodation or a modest sub-group, not relocation of the committed campus symposium. The supplied 20–120-room commercial band is a selling constraint, not a forecast. No 2027 attendance or room demand is published in reviewed sources, so neither a room-block target nor meeting-capacity fit can be qualified. No resort requirement is evidenced. Do not position this as downtown-Geneva, Lausanne or Palexpo overflow.
findings.venueCommitments: Agroscope’s edition-specific calendar explicitly lists Location: Changins. Hosts are OENOVITI International, Agroscope and UAS Changins. This is an academic/research-site event in Nyon / La Côte, Vaud, not downtown Geneva or Lausanne and not a competing hotel. Changins school address is Route du Duillier 52, CH-1260 Nyon; Agroscope’s Changins site address is Route de Duillier 60, 1260 Nyon. Exact event building/room and allocation between the two sites are not established; these addresses must not be collapsed into one confirmed meeting address. No signed venue contract is evidenced.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified rotation: Japan (Kyoto, Yamanashi/Kofu and Niigata), 11–15 May 2023; Asti, Italy, 14–15 May 2024; Vienna, Austria, 22–23 May 2025; Porto, Portugal, 20–22 May 2026; Nyon, Switzerland, 19–21 May 2027. Official network text expressly describes annual Symposium and General Assembly events. Annual recurrence is verified, but a recurring Swiss destination or 2028 Swiss return is not.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Participant self-booking, not an evidenced centrally contracted room block or housing bureau. Official OENOVITI quote: "OENOVITI Members will need to make their own accommodation bookings". The only 2027 hotel named is Hôtel B&B NYON, 20 Allée de la Petite Prairie, 1260 Nyon, with participant identification code NOVITI27. OENOVITI states: "Activities will depart and return to this location." Agroscope explicitly adds: "You are, of course, free to choose alternative accommodation to suit your needs." No published allotment size, guaranteed inventory, negotiated rate, room nights, release date or open RFP was found. The code is not evidence of a contracted block.
findings.organizationStructure: OENOVITI is an international academic/industry viticulture and oenology network, administered by an Executive Committee and supported by its Bordeaux-based ISVV Coordination Office. ADERA manages network finances, membership fee collection and project-management support; this is not evidence of a hotel-buying mandate. Changins and Agroscope are local institutional co-hosts, not a hotel or an identified PCO/DMC. The supplied corporate-meetings segment should be reviewed: the evidenced event is a scientific symposium plus network general assembly.
findings.competitiveLimitations: B&B Nyon is an edition-specific recommended incumbent accommodation option and the published activity departure/return point. That creates a practical disadvantage for a Founex alternative. It does not establish exclusive hotel commitment: alternative accommodation is explicitly permitted. No B&B sell-out, capacity constraint, rejected demand or overflow evidence was found; do not claim overflow.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact the OENOVITI Coordination Office, for Pierre-Louis Teissedre, and Isabel Baehler at Changins before the published 1 December 2026 registration opening. Ask who manages local logistics, whether an additional optional hotel may be communicated to delegates, whether B&B Nyon has any guaranteed/exclusive commitment, expected residential attendance and stay pattern, and how a Founex alternative could connect to the pickup point. Only then offer a capped, release-date-based group rate or participant booking link. Do not request a symposium-venue replacement or imply an active RFP.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: The May 2027 edition is upcoming. Alternative participant-paid accommodation is explicitly accessible in principle, but no open organizer hotel procurement is verified. YOTEL is not listed and no YOTEL pickup or transfer is evidenced. Any group proposal depends on organizer permission, participant interest and a workable transfer arrangement to Changins/B&B Nyon. Registration is scheduled to open 1 December 2026.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: prioritize a 2027 alternative-lodging relationship with the local hosts and central coordination office. International rotation means future annual editions are not automatically La Côte hotel opportunities. A later Swiss host cycle or separate locally hosted workshop could justify early accommodation positioning only after destination and host confirmation; no such future local edition is presently verified.
